vista.name: Legacy Update 1.14.1
vista.signer: CN=Hashbang Productions, O=Hashbang Productions, L=Adelaide, S=South Australia, C=AU
vista.licence: open source (LegacyUpdate/LegacyUpdate, GPL per manifests.json note); free, donations
vista.notes: Legacy Update 1.14.1 (GitHub release 2026-10-22, source GPL/open). Unofficial community project, NOT Microsoft. Supports Windows 2000 SP4, XP, Vista, 7, 8, 8.1 (and Server 2003-2012 R2); installs missing Service Packs, servicing stacks, SHA-2 updates (7: KB4474419, KB4490628), Windows Update Agent, updates the trusted root/disallowed certificate store from Microsoft's trustedr SST files (all versions up to 8.1), and enables TLS 1.1/1.2 in SChannel, WinHTTP DefaultSecureProtocols, IE SecureProtocols and .NET SystemDefaultTlsVersions (Easy-Fix equivalent). Since 1.14 it also uses its own Windows Update proxy on 7+ because Windows Update certificates expire June 2027. Free (donations). Switches from legacyupdate.net/help/flags: /S silent (case-sensitive, exit 3010 if restart needed), /norestart, /passive (1.10+, default options, shows UI). legacyupdate.net returns HTTP 403 to automated clients, switches confirmed via search snippet of that page and setup.nsi source. On XP its optional 'Windows Embedded POSReady 2009 updates' feature must stay OFF (licence trick, forbidden for Charon). XP note: if setup does nothing, see legacyupdate.net/help/nothing-happens (signature bug in XP). Vista: the LegacyUpdate README says the ActiveX control was 'forward-ported' to add support for Windows Vista and later (it also restores Vista Ultimate Extras); it applies Microsoft trustedr root updates on Vista too. Vista needs SP2. Its Server 2008 / POSReady-type optional updates, if offered, must stay OFF for Charon. Same file as legacy-update-7 (not downloaded again). read 2026-11-25

vista.name: Microsoft trusted root certificate list (authroots.sst)
vista.licence: Microsoft certificate trust list data (Windows Update static file)
vista.notes: Official Microsoft certificate trust list file, the same source Legacy Update's UpdateRoots step uses (TRUSTEDR constant). Served by Microsoft over HTTP only (HTTPS on download/ctldl.windowsupdate.com does not answer), so verify by hash; it is a ROLLING file that Microsoft updates several times a year, so the hash is valid only for the copy fetched 2026-11-25. Not a PE file, no Authenticode signer recorded. Legacy Update installs authroots/updroots into AuthRoot, roots into Root, removes delroots, adds disallowedcert to Disallowed (no separate silent installer: apply through Legacy Update, or certutil -addstore where certutil exists, i.e. 7/8/8.1). Not Authenticode-signed (signer empty). Vista: same Microsoft file and hash as the -7 entry in manifests.json (not downloaded again); apply through legacy-update-vista. read 2026-11-25

95.name: Charon Hypervisor TLS proxy
95.notes: Needed on Windows 95: no TLS 1.2/1.3 in the system (IE5/IE6 WinInet/SChannel offer at most SSL 3.0/TLS 1.0) and CryptoAPI has no SHA-2, so no Microsoft root-store update can make modern HTTPS work; there is no clean-origin root certificate updater for 9x (the trustedr SST files need XP SP3+ CryptoAPI). The hypervisor's own TLS proxy terminates modern TLS on the host side; nothing third-party is installed in the guest. The only maintained TLS-capable browser found, RetroZilla 2.3, is recorded in manifests-9x.json (retrozilla-95; Defender quarantine there). read 2026-11-25
